Hadamard transform (H⊗n)

Words: 201 Articles: 5
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
The normalized Hadamard transform maps a vector indexed by binary strings through entries 2−n/2(−1)x⋅y. It is its own inverse and an orthogonal transform. The Hadamard gate is the n=1 quantum case, and the Hadamard basis is the image of its computational basis. The Walsh-Hadamard transform gives the same tensor-power construction.

Hadamard gate

Words: 115 Articles: 2
Hadamard transform OurBigBook.com
The Hadamard gate maps
∣0⟩↦2​∣0⟩+∣1⟩​,∣1⟩↦2​∣0⟩−∣1⟩​.
(1)

Photon-number reference for a Hadamard gate (rk​=1−1/k,sk​=max(k−2,0)/k)

Words: 95
Hadamard gate OurBigBook.com
A flat reference over k adjacent Fock states has overlap rk​ with a one-photon shift and sk​ with a two-photon shift. These overlaps, obtained by counting shared number states, determine the reduced qubit channel of a number-conserving Hadamard interaction. For k≥2, its squared fidelity with the desired pure output is 1−(1+xz)/(2k) for input Bloch vector (x,y,z). Its worst-case infidelity is 3/(4k) because ∣xz∣≤1/2. At k=1 the two-shift overlap is zero, not −1, and the fidelity is 1/2+(y2−xz)/4. Broad coherent number support, rather than merely a large fixed photon number, suppresses distinguishability of the outgoing field states.

Uniform quantum superposition

Words: 13
Hadamard gate OurBigBook.com
The uniform superposition of all n-bit strings is
2n​1​∑x∈{0,1}n​∣x⟩=H⊗n∣0⟩⊗n.
(2)

Walsh-Hadamard transform (H⊗n)

Words: 30
Hadamard transform OurBigBook.com
On n qubits, the Walsh-Hadamard transform satisfies
H⊗n∣x⟩=2−n/2∑y∈{0,1}n​(−1)x⋅y∣y⟩,
(3)
where the dot product is evaluated modulo two.
This is the Hadamard transform acting on the computational basis of n qubits.

Hadamard basis

Words: 10
Hadamard transform OurBigBook.com
The qubit Hadamard basis consists of ∣+⟩=(∣0⟩+∣1⟩)/2​ and ∣−⟩=(∣0⟩−∣1⟩)/2​.

Minimal coupling

Words: 60 Articles: 1
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
Minimal coupling introduces a gauge potential through a covariant derivative, or replaces canonical momentum by p−qA. The associated scalar potential supplies the electric coupling. Magnetic minimal coupling is the magnetic-only nonrelativistic case.

Magnetic minimal coupling

Words: 30
Minimal coupling OurBigBook.com
For a particle of charge q in a vector potential A, the canonical momentum in the free Hamiltonian is replaced by p−qA, giving
H=2m1​(−iℏ∇−qA)2.
(4)

Quantum fluctuation (⟨(O−⟨O⟩)2⟩)

Words: 44
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum fluctuation is a nonzero variance of an observable in a quantum state, even when its mean vanishes. A vacuum field mode has such zero-point variance. In an inflationary background, the expanding geometry transfers short-wavelength vacuum field fluctuations into primordial perturbations as their wavelengths cross the Hubble radius.

Gauge covariance of the Schrödinger equation

Words: 26
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
For a particle of charge −e, the changes A↦A+∇f and ϕ↦ϕ−∂t​f leave the minimally coupled Schrödinger equation invariant when ψ↦e−ief/ℏψ.

Amplitude amplification

Words: 377 Articles: 6
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
If a state has good amplitude sinθ, the product of the reflection in the bad axis and the reflection in the state line rotates its good-bad plane by 2θ. After k iterations the good probability is
sin2((2k+1)θ),
(5)
so O(1/sinθ) iterations raise a small good amplitude close to one.

Nearest-integer stopping for amplitude amplification (r=⌊π/(4θ)⌋,sin2θ=p)

Words: 49
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
For known initial success probability p∈(0,1), this choice of iteration count ensures ∣(2r+1)θ−π/2∣≤θ. Hence the success probability after amplitude amplification is at least cos2θ=1−p. Counting initial state preparation and the forward and inverse preparation in each iterate gives 2r+1 preparation-unitary applications, asymptotic to π/(2p​) as p→0.

Two-dimensional matrix for phase amplitude amplification (Q=−[I+(eiϕ−1)∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣]diag(eiθ,1))

Words: 71
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
If the state-preparation unitary sends ∣0⟩ to ∣ψ⟩=sinχ∣g⟩+cosχ∣b⟩, use the orthonormal good/bad basis. The marked-space phase is diagonal there, and conjugating a phase on ∣0⟩ gives the rank-one phase in the displayed formula. Their product is unitary. An arbitrary preparation unitary not sending zero to this state need not preserve this particular two-dimensional subspace. Matrices in unnormalized good/bad vectors must not be described as unitary in the ordinary Euclidean inner product.

Exact amplitude amplification

Words: 181 Articles: 2
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
If the initial good amplitude p=sinθ is known, an ancillary qubit can reduce it to sinθ′=pc with θ′=π/(4k+2) and 0<c≤1. After k ordinary amplitude-amplification iterations the good amplitude is sin((2k+1)θ′)=1, so the target state is prepared exactly.

Known-state success dilution for exact amplitude amplification (p∗​=sin2[π/(4j+2)]≤p)

Words: 101
Exact amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
For known good probability p=sin2θ, choose j=⌈π/(4θ)−1/2⌉. A known reversible preparation of one state with good probability p∗​ permits j ordinary amplitude amplification iterations to reach the good subspace exactly. With ancillary marking access, prepare a flag with one-probability q=p∗​/p and define joint success as good data and flag one. Reflection about the prepared product state is known, while the joint phase test requires a controlled marking oracle or a computed Boolean output. This changes the success projector and enlarges the state space; it does not evade the obstruction to uniform probability lowering by a unitary. Query costs of preparation, its inverse and marking must all be counted.

Phase-matched amplitude amplification

Words: 40
Exact amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
Phase-matched amplitude amplification replaces the two sign-flip reflections by selective phase rotations. Choosing their phases from the known initial overlap can rotate the state exactly onto the target even when an integer number of ordinary Grover rotations would overshoot it.

Geometric amplitude-amplification schedule

Words: 26
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
A geometric amplitude-amplification schedule tries iteration counts 1,2,4,8,… when the initial good amplitude is unknown. It reaches the unknown optimal scale with only a geometric-series overhead.

Let a real function h obey ∣h(λj​)∣≤1, and assume the required quantum variable rotations are available. Coherent exact quantum phase estimation, a quantum variable rotation and uncomputation implement
∣uj​⟩∣0⟩⟼∣uj​⟩(1−h(λj​)2​∣0⟩+h(λj​)∣1⟩).

Postselection on flag one gives h(A)∣b⟩ normalized, with probability ∥h(A)∣b⟩∥2, provided this vector is nonzero. Erasing the eigenvalue label by uncomputation is essential to preserve coherence between different eigenvectors. On this dyadic spectrum, U2t=I gives U−1=U2t−1, so reversing the phase-estimation gates is possible using forward controlled-U calls. The choice h(λ)=λ multiplies by A; a scaled reciprocal gives the different filter used in the HHL algorithm.

Quantum decoherence

Words: 519 Articles: 10
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
Quantum decoherence is the suppression of observable phase coherence when a system becomes entangled with unobserved environmental degrees of freedom. In a preferred basis, tracing out the environment damps off-diagonal entries of the system's reduced density matrix while leaving the corresponding populations unchanged.

An initially aligned bath leaves the overlap's modulus at one. Initially equatorial spins yield zN​(t)=∏k​cos(2gk​t). Global unitary time evolution remains reversible, and a finite spin-bath coherence recurrence prevents a strict zero long-time limit at finite bath size.

Ensemble spin-bath coherence supplies exact mean and mean-square formulas for a uniform coupling distribution, while short-time Gaussian spin-bath decoherence gives the initial decay scale.

On the scale t=O((g∗​N​)−1), the total fourth-order remainder tends to zero, giving the Gaussian coherence envelope. Foundations of quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A superselection rule partitions a representation into sectors between which the specified observable algebra has no matrix elements. Relative phases between vectors in different sectors cannot be detected by those observables, so a coherent vector spanning sectors and its sector-diagonal mixture define the same observable state. The restriction is relative to the observable algebra; it is not by itself a physical wave-function collapse. Infinite-system phases can yield disjoint representations and emergent superselection sectors even though each finite system permits global connecting operators.

The certainty of a prediction made without disturbing the system is proposed as sufficient evidence that the predicted quantity corresponds to an element of physical reality. It motivates the discussion of completeness and locality in foundations of quantum mechanics, but is distinct from the conditional factorization assumed by local hidden-variable theory.

An ontological model associates each quantum state preparation with a probability distribution over underlying physical states λ. A measurement in quantum mechanics's response probabilities depend on its specification and λ, sum to one, and reproduce the Born rule when averaged over the preparation distribution. The model need not assign deterministic outcomes. Overlap or disjointness of preparation measures defines the psi-epistemic model versus psi-ontic model distinction.

Under preparation independence, an ontological model of a quantum system reproducing exact quantum measurement in quantum mechanics probabilities cannot assign overlapping preparation measures to distinct pure states. An exclusion measurement in quantum mechanics on independent copies makes every outcome impossible for one possible preparation; a common ontic region would require every response to vanish there. Thus the conclusion is a psi-ontic model, not a blanket exclusion of hidden variables or all informational interpretations.

Applying the two-block PBR exclusion measurement for zero and plus uses 2n independently prepared copies. A common single-copy ontic overlap of positive mass remains positive under this finite tensor power.

Each vector has zero inner product with its labelled preparation. This projective measurement gives antidistinguishable quantum states and drives the two-copy PBR theorem contradiction.

Independently operated quantum state preparations are assumed to produce independent underlying physical states. Their joint preparation measure factors into the single-system measures. This ontic factorization is an additional assumption, not a consequence of operational independence alone. It turns a common single-system overlap of mass ε into a common n-system overlap of mass εn in the PBR theorem.

Ontological model of a quantum system OurBigBook.com
An ontological model of a quantum system is psi-epistemic if some pair of distinct pure states has preparation measures with nonzero overlap. The same physical state can then be compatible with either preparation. This precise measure-overlap definition is stronger than merely interpreting a wave function as information or a computational tool.

An ontological model of a quantum system is psi-ontic if distinct pure states have mutually singular preparation distributions. The physical state then determines which pure quantum state was prepared, almost surely in the pairwise sense. Extra underlying variables may still exist. The PBR theorem establishes this conclusion under preparation independence and exact quantum predictions.

If the localized operator misses a second observable's support, their commutation and the exact ground-state bra identity convert the connected correlation function into an approximation error. The two-projection power estimate yields spatial decay rate α=31​ln(1+Δ/2) for the stated detectability contraction.
Frustration freeness (E0​(H)=∑Z​E0​(hZ​))
Words: 42
Frustration-free quantum Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A decomposition H=∑Z​hZ​ has frustration freeness when a global ground state minimizes every term simultaneously. For finite-dimensional Hermitian terms this implies E0​(H)=∑Z​E0​(hZ​). Shifting each term by its minimum produces positive operators with a common null vector. The property depends on the decomposition, not only the total operator.

k-local Hamiltonian (k-local Hamiltonian)

Words: 28
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A k-local Hamiltonian is a sum of terms that each act nontrivially on at most k subsystems. The integer k remains fixed as the system size grows.

Product-formula Hamiltonian simulation

Words: 97 Articles: 2
Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
Product-formula Hamiltonian simulation approximates e−it(A+B) by alternating exponentials of A and B, which are assumed easier to implement separately.

First-order two-local Hamiltonian simulation (O(M+M3t2/ϵ))

Words: 53
Product-formula Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
For a sum of M Hermitian two-local terms of norm below one, repeat a first-order Lie-Trotter product formula step r times. The first-order unitary product-formula error bound gives total error at most t2∑j<k​∥[Hj​,Hk​]∥/(2r)<M(M−1)t2/(2r) for M>1. Taking r=max(1,⌈M(M−1)t2/(2ϵ)⌉) uses Mr arbitrary two-qubit gates. At unit time and M=O(n2) this is a sufficient O(n6/ϵ) bound; additional commutation structure can improve it.

The symmetric second-order formula, also called Strang splitting, is
e−iδA/2e−iδBe−iδA/2=e−iδ(A+B)+O(δ3)
(99)
for bounded operators, with the constant controlled by nested commutators.

Simulation of a computable diagonal Hamiltonian

Words: 120 Articles: 1
Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
Let A∣x⟩=a(x)∣x⟩, where a reversible circuit C computes a(x) into a clean register. Then applying e−ita(x) as a phase on that register and performing uncomputation implements e−itA on the data register. For a(x)=(−1)f(x), a Boolean output qubit suffices: C†(I⊗e−itZ)C acts as e−itA when that qubit starts in ∣0⟩. This exact construction avoids a Lie-Trotter product formula because the eigenvalue is computed directly.

Pauli-string phase by parity computation (eitZ⊗n)

Words: 60
Simulation of a computable diagonal Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
The Pauli Z gates give eigenvalue (−1)∑j​xj​ on ∣x⟩. Use parity computation by CNOT gates to put the parity bit in a zero ancilla, apply eitZ to it, and uncompute. The data acquire exactly eit(−1)∑j​xj​, and the ancillary line returns to zero. This compute-phase-uncompute construction needs 2n+1 one- and two-qubit gates. Accumulating parity into the last data line instead uses 2n−1 gates without an extra ancilla. Neither implementation drops the global phase.

Block encoding

Words: 36
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
A block encoding of a matrix A is a unitary operator whose designated block equals A/α for a known normalization factor α. It gives a quantum circuit coherent access to matrices that need not themselves be unitary.
